$comment: Historical secret-scan findings, each already judged.
`pnpm security:secrets:history` walks every commit, so it finds values that were
removed from the working tree long ago and are reachable only through `git log`.
A finding listed here is reported and does not fail the scan; anything NOT listed
fails. An entry that no longer occurs is printed as a note, so the file can shrink.
Every row needs a `why` that names why the value is not a live credential. A row
without one is filtered out of the baseline and therefore fails the scan, which is
the intended direction: an unexplained exception is not an exception.
Keyed on the exact pair the scanner prints — the path, and the human-readable
shape. A finding in a *different* shape in the *same* file is a new finding.

findings.why: A localhost compose password, replaced by the `POSTGRES_HOST_AUTH_METHOD: trust` service pattern the CI workflows use. The current file has no inline password; this is the pre-rewrite revision. Rotating it would change nothing, because the database it pointed at only ever existed on a developer's machine.
The same localhost compose password in a second, older compose file, on the same reasoning as `docker-compose.unified.yml`.
A helper that set `DATABASE_URL` to the same localhost password. The current script reads it from the environment.
The PowerShell twin of the same helper, on the same reasoning.

An example environment file that used `automate:automate` rather than the tree's `user:pass` placeholder convention. The convention was adopted after this file was written; the file is now allowlisted by path in `isAllowlistedPath`, and this row covers the revision before that.

An early CI service definition that passed a password to the postgres service. Every postgres service in the current workflows uses `POSTGRES_HOST_AUTH_METHOD: trust` with a comment saying why a password there would itself be a committed credential. Same local-only database.

A test fixture that hard-coded a webhook-shaped string instead of assembling one at runtime, which is the same defect `apps/api/src/test-support/synthetic-credentials.ts` exists to prevent. The test no longer contains the literal.

Captured tool output under `.sisyphus/`, recording the `docker compose config` dump that contained the compose password above. Generated evidence, not source, and the file it captured has since been rewritten.

A SAML test fixture holding a PEM-shaped block. Synthetic, never loaded by a SAML library in a way that would accept it, and the file is not part of any workspace package. Worth removing for its own sake — recorded here rather than silently tolerated so that the removal is a tracked task.

A hardening check's own fixture, asserting that a live-key-shaped value is detected. The value is a fixture, and the test is the detector's proof — deleting it would remove the evidence that the detector works. Reassembled at runtime in the current file.
An AI-provider schema fixture asserting that an AWS-key-shaped value is rejected. Same reasoning as the Stripe row: it is the detector's proof rather than a credential.
